newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: -- All contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Tuesday, with turnover rising to 12.49 million lots from 10.2 million.
The annual rate for the three-day contract soared to 21.75 percent from 12.15 percent on Monday and the most active seven-day contract rose to 13.50 percent from 11.98 percent.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the rises, in particular of early-maturing contracts, were mainly due to new domestic A share issues in Shanghai this week, which attracted funds from the repo market. The rates will face profit-taking pressure after sharp gains.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed down across the board, with volume rising to 3.38 million lots from 2.12 million.
The most active three-year bond that matures in August 1999 closed down at 104.83 yuan from 105.16 yuan and the 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 122.20 yuan from 122.80.
Traders said the sharp falls were due to the new A share issues and market expectations of lower returns on T-bonds.
"Many investors believe returns of the T-bonds will come down with the fall in inflation," said a trader.
